newsitem.title: BELGIUM: NATO agrees to boost Bosnian force for civic polls.
newsitem.headline: NATO agrees to boost Bosnian force for civic polls.

text.p: Countries taking part in the NATO-led peace force in Bosnia agreed on Friday to send about 3,000 more troops to the country to help with the organisation of muncipal elections on September 13-14.

Sixteen NATO countries and 20 non-NATO countries meeting in Brussels for a six-month review of the Stabilisation Force (SFOR) approved a request from military commanders for an additional six battalions, about 3,000 troops.

Describing the municipal elections as a milestone in implementing the Dayton peace agreement on Bosnia, they said in a statement that the SFOR would provide the general security framework for the elections as well as other direct support to the Organisation for Security and Cooperation in Europe (OSCE).
The statement, released after the talks, added that most of the help for the OSCE, which is running the poll would be in the form of communications and logistics.
The elections, which have been postponed twice, are seen as essential if refugees and displaced people forced to flee their homes through ethnic cleansing are to return.
SFOR currently has around 35,000 troops in Bosnia, helping to ensure implementation of the Dayton accords which ended the 3-1/2 year war.
The force took over from the alliance-led Implementation Force which at its height totalled 60,000 troops. It is due to leave Bosnia in June 1998.
